# Introduction

In this vignette, we demonstrate how to use the NESMR package for plotting and visualizing network structures inferred from GWAS summary statistics.
We provide a simulation example, perform network discovery, and illustrate various plotting functions available in the package.


## Simulation Example

We simulate GWAS summary statistics for traits that have a specified network structure using [GWASBrewer](https://github.com/jean997/GWASBrewer).

```{r}
set.seed(13)
library(esmr)
library(GWASBrewer)
G <- matrix(
  c(0, 0, 0, 0,
    0.25, 0, 0, 0,
    0, 0, 0,  0,
    0, -0.15, 0.2, 0),
  nrow = 4,
  byrow = 4
)

d <- ncol(G)

B_full <- matrix(1, d, d)
B_lower <- lower.tri(G) + 0
B_correct <- (G != 0) + 0

h2 <- 0.2
J <- 5000
N <- 20000
pi_J <- 0.1
alpha <- 5e-8

dat <- sim_mv(
    G = G,
    N = N,
    J = J,
    h2 = h2,
    pi = pi_J,
    sporadic_pleiotropy = TRUE,
    est_s = TRUE
)
```

## Discovery

We start the chain from a graph far from the truth, with every true edge reversed, so the diagnostic plots below show the chain moving toward the best graph.

```{r}
suppressWarnings(capture.output(
  mh_results <- mh_graph_explore(dat, starting_graph = t(B_correct)),
  file = nullfile()
))

kableExtra::kable(
  head(discovery_summary(mh_results), n = 10),
  digits = 4)
```

### Discovery Plots - ELBO

```{r norm-elbo-plots, fig.height = 6}
library(ggplot2)

plot(mh_results, plot_type = "norm_elbo")
plot(mh_results, plot_type = "cum_norm_elbo")
plot(mh_results, plot_type = "both")
```

## Individual Graph Plots

Individual graph objects extend [tidygraphs](https://tidygraph.data-imaginist.com/) which provide an easy interface that works with [ggraph](https://ggraph.data-imaginist.com/index.html) for plotting.

We can get the best graph from the discovery results.

```{r best-graph}
best_graph <- top_i_graph(mh_results)

print(best_graph)
```

### Adjacency Graph

Plot trinary graph (+1,0,-1) for positive and negative effects

```{r best-graph-adj}
plot_layered_topo(best_graph)
```

### Weighted Graph

```{r best-graph-beta}
plot_layered_topo(best_graph, plot_type = "beta", weight = "direct_effect")
```

### Weighted Graph - Tile

The default plot for the weighted adjacency matrix plots the the tiles in matrix ordering. This can be controlled with the `x_axis_position` argument which accepts `top` or `bottom`.
The variables are topologically ordered by default in the same order as the `plot_layered_topo` function.

```{r tile-best-graph-beta}
plot_nesmr_tile(best_graph, x_axis_position = "top", node_order = 4:1)
```

```{r, tile-best-graph-beta-bottom}
plot_nesmr_tile(best_graph, x_axis_position = "bottom", node_order = 4:1)
```

### Edge Inclusion Probabilities - Tile

Edge inclusion probabilities are the approximate posterior inclusion probability, or the sum of all of the normalized ELBOs in which that edge is present in a graph.

```{r eip-tile-plot}
edge_inclusion_tile_plot(mh_results, node_order = 4:1)
```

### Tile plots from the discovery object

`plot_nesmr_tile()` also accepts the discovery object directly. The `type` argument selects what to plot, and every type orders the nodes by the best graph unless `node_order` is given.

| `type` | Plot |
|---|---|
| `"edge_inc_prob"` | Edge inclusion probabilities |
| `"best"` | Direct effects of the best graph |
| `"total"` | Total effects of the best graph |
| `"indirect"` | Indirect effects (total - direct) of the best graph |
| `"start"` | Direct effects of the graph the chain started from |
| `"proposal_freq"` | Frequency of each edge among the proposed graphs |

```{r tile-types, fig.width = 5, fig.height = 5}
plot_nesmr_tile(mh_results, type = "best")
plot_nesmr_tile(mh_results, type = "total")
plot_nesmr_tile(mh_results, type = "indirect")
plot_nesmr_tile(mh_results, type = "start")
plot_nesmr_tile(mh_results, type = "proposal_freq")
```

The starting graph is available as a graph with `discovery_start_graph()`.

### Labels and layout

Nodes are named by their position unless `labels` is supplied, one label per node. Additional arguments are passed on to the tile plot:
`lower_tri_only` only draws grid lines for the lower triangle (useful for DAGs), `x_axis_at` chooses the side of the x-axis labels, and `x_text_angle` rotates them.

```{r tile-labels, fig.width = 5, fig.height = 5}
trait_names <- c("Trait A", "Trait B", "Trait C", "Trait D")

plot_nesmr_tile(
  mh_results, type = "total", labels = trait_names,
  lower_tri_only = TRUE, x_axis_at = "bottom", x_text_angle = 30
)
edge_inclusion_tile_plot(
  mh_results, labels = trait_names, x_axis_at = "bottom", x_text_angle = 30
)
```

## Graph Differences

We can compare the different graphs returned from NESMR discovery using a few different plotting function.

### Graph Differences - Beta difference

```{r graph-diff-plot, fig.width = 10, fig.height = 5}
library(gridExtra)
best_graph <- top_i_graph(mh_results)
next_graph <- top_i_graph(mh_results, i = 2)

coords <- layered_topo_sort_coords(best_graph)
p1 <- plot_nesmr_graph(best_graph, coords = coords, plot_type = "beta") + ggtitle("Best Graph")
p2 <- plot_nesmr_graph(next_graph, coords = coords, plot_type = "beta") + ggtitle("Next Graph")
grid.arrange(p1, p2, nrow = 1)
```

We can use the `-` operation on graphs to compute the differences between the graphs.
This returns a tidygraph object which has edge comparisons for each edge in both graphs.
These are columns in the tidygraph edges:

  - `adj_diff` Adjacency difference. For a single graph, an edge present is considered a 1 and missing is considered zero. Then `adj_diff` is subtraction from these binary variables resulting in possible values of -1, 0, 1 representing edge in second graph only, edge present or absent in both graphs, or edge present in first graph only
  - `sign_diff` Differences in the signs of the effects
    - `-2 = "Sign Flip: - → +"`
    - `-1 = "Edge Removed"`
    - `0 = "No Change"`
    - `1 = "Edge Added"`
    - `2 = "Sign Flip: + → -"`
  - `direct_effect` is now the difference of effects

```{r graph-diff}
print(best_graph - next_graph)
```

These differences can be plotted in matrix/tile plotting functions

```{r graph-diff-plot-beta}
plot_graph_differences(best_graph, next_graph, diff_type = "beta", node_order = 4:1)
```

```{r graph-diff-plot-adj}
# Adjacency (edge presence) differences
plot_graph_differences(best_graph, next_graph, diff_type = "adj", node_order = 4:1)
```

Both graphs can be relabeled with `labels`. Here we compare the best graph to the graph the chain started from.

```{r graph-diff-start}
plot_graph_differences(
  best_graph, discovery_start_graph(mh_results),
  diff_type = "adj", labels = trait_names
)
```

## MH Chain Diagnostics

The following plots summarize the Metropolis-Hastings exploration. Points are colored by the type of move that proposed the graph.

### Trace plots

`plot_mh_trace()` plots one of the following against the MH iteration (`x_axis = "iter"`) or the number of unique graphs fit (`x_axis = "graph_fit"`):

  - `"elbo"`: ELBO of each new graph relative to the best, with the accepted state of the chain in grey
  - `"exp_elbo"`: the same on the exponential scale
  - `"cum_best_elbo"`: the best ELBO found so far
  - `"cum_total_elbo"`: the cumulative total exp(ELBO) explored
  - `"new_best"`: the iterations that discovered a new best graph

```{r mh-trace, fig.height = 5}
plot_mh_trace(mh_results, "elbo")
plot_mh_trace(mh_results, "exp_elbo")
plot_mh_trace(mh_results, "cum_best_elbo")
plot_mh_trace(mh_results, "cum_total_elbo", x_axis = "graph_fit")
plot_mh_trace(mh_results, "new_best")
```

### Distance of the current best graph to the overall best

`plot_mh_best_path()` follows each new best graph found during the chain and plots its distance to the overall best graph: the edit distance between graphs (`"edit_distance"`), the ELBO difference (`"elbo_diff"`), or the Frobenius norm of the difference in direct effects (`"frob_norm"`).
Moves that improve the ELBO by more than `label_gain` are annotated when the ggrepel package is installed; set `label_gain = NULL` to turn this off.

```{r mh-best-path, fig.height = 5}
plot_mh_best_path(mh_results, "edit_distance", labels = trait_names)
plot_mh_best_path(mh_results, "elbo_diff", label_gain = NULL)
plot_mh_best_path(mh_results, "frob_norm", label_gain = NULL)
```

### Acceptance rate

Cumulative and rolling acceptance and new-graph rates. Dashed lines mark the start of a new chain.

```{r mh-accept-rate, fig.height = 7}
plot_mh_accept_rate(mh_results, window = 25)
```
